explanations.3: This line describes what the tool does: it reads Bash scripts and checks them against best practices without ever modifying files (read-only).
explanations.10: The backticks around `bash-best-practices` indicate it's referring to a specific document or rule set that should be read first to understand what violations look like.
explanations.23: Default means 'if no other instruction is given, do this'; in this case, look at all shell scripts under the standard directories unless the project specifies different folders.
explanations.33: This command finds all shell files and checks if they contain the safety line; the `||` means 'or' — if grep doesn't find the line, echo a warning.
explanations.36: When grep searches but finds nothing, it returns exit code 1 (failure), which under `set -euo pipefail` stops the entire script; adding `|| true` says 'that's okay, keep going'.
explanations.43: This command lists line counts for shell files and shows only those with more than 300 lines; it's a quick way to find scripts that might be too large.
